title: Ruum-User token claims
description: The claims of the signed token that the app gateway sends to an app in the header `Ruum-User` (docs/DESIGN.md section 9.4; the design text calls it `Platform-User`). A JWT (EdDSA) signed with the platform's app-token keys (`<issuer>/.well-known/app-jwks.json`, a key set apart from the API keys). The app checks it with the Ruum SDK: signature, `iss` = `RUUM_ISSUER`, `aud` = `RUUM_AUDIENCE` (its own app ID, or for a preview the preview audience), `typ` = `app_user`, `env` = `RUUM_ENV`, `exp`. It holds only the facts this app may know. It is made for each request (or cached for at most 5 seconds), so a removed role stops working at once; the app should not keep its own copy of roles. The same format identifies calls from other apps (`actor: app`, design 9.10) and from partners (`actor: partner`). **Open for later steps** (contracts/apps/README.md): apps and the SDK ignore claims they do not know and accept unknown values of `actor` and new `sub` prefixes; they never reject a token for an extra claim. DRAFT for review (step 3 specify phase, docs/STEP3.md).

iss.description: The origin of the Ruum instance that signed the token (`https://ruum.space`; the laptop stack `https://ruum.localhost`; a self-hosted instance its own origin). The SDK compares it with `RUUM_ISSUER`, which the runtime sets.

aud.description: Live: `app:<app-node-id>`. A preview: `app:<app-node-id>/preview/<deployment-id>`, so a token that a preview received never passes the live app's check (review R3). The runtime sets `RUUM_AUDIENCE` to the value the app must accept.

env.description: Must match `RUUM_ENV` of the receiving app.

sub.description: `pairwise:<id>`: a person or an agent, stable for this app and different for every other app, so two apps cannot join their user lists. `app:<id>`: a calling app of the same tenant. `partner:<key-id>`: a partner API key. `anonymous:<visit>`: a visitor of a public app without sign-in (the visit that the gateway issued). Later steps may add prefixes (federation: `remote:`); apps treat an unknown prefix as an opaque ID.

name.description: Only if the manifest asks (`claims`) and the tenant allows.

email.description: Only if the manifest asks and the tenant allows (never for public apps by default).

roles.description: The app roles of the visitor (design 9.3): explicit grants of active roles, or the default role for a visitor with `view` and no explicit role. Empty for anonymous visitors and partners.

node_roles.description: The visitor's effective rights on the bound nodes, by binding name, for UI decisions (`{"db": "edit"}`). Not a grant: the app's own access goes through its bindings.

actor.description: Who sends the request. Known values: `user`, `agent` (an agent acting for a user; its user's pairwise ID is `on_behalf_of`; in step 3 only on preview hosts), `app`, `partner`, `anonymous`. An open set: apps treat an unknown value like `anonymous` for their own decisions.

on_behalf_of.description: The user that an agent or a calling app acts for (a delegation chain, design 9.10).

chain.description: The apps of a delegation chain, oldest first (user → app A → app B: B sees `["app:<A>"]`).

scopes.description: For `app` and `partner` actors: the API scopes of the binding or the key.
